# CTA frequency

**How often do posts ask for something or sell?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C18, C10


## A keyword CTA on nearly every reel
<a id="every-reel"></a>

Every reel ends with a comment keyword and a freebie.

**Looks like:** Ten reels in ten days, each ending on its own big yellow keyword (75K, CPU, GMAIL). The audience learns that every reel has something to collect.

**Good at:** steady comments; a big DM list; habit for the audience

**Weak at:** can feel salesy; a freebie to make every time

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90 · niches tech, all · goals comments, sales · effort medium

**How:** Keep a keyword plus freebie template in HyperFrames, and a resource folder ready for DMs.

**Backed by:** [Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta), [Keyword CTA: ~10× more comments](../topics/growth.md#growth-keyword-cta-comment-gap), [Lead-magnet CTA over a recap strip](../topics/growth.md#l11-lead-magnet-recap-cta), [Caption: hook line, story, CTA, 3–5 tags](../topics/text.md#text-caption-structure), [Weekly lead magnet into an owned list](../topics/growth.md#growth-lead-magnet-series) · sources R1, L01

## Weekly rhythm: 4 reach, 2 deep, 1 sell
<a id="weekly-rhythm"></a>

Most posts are reach or value; one a week sells. Stories sell twice a week, the rest is life.

**Looks like:** Four wide, relatable reels with no ask, two deep breakdowns with a soft ask, and one 'sneak peek inside' post with a clear offer. Stories sell on Tuesday and Friday.

**Good at:** trust; reach not hurt by selling; clear jobs per post

**Weak at:** fewer leads per week; needs planning

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, story, carousel · niches all · goals trust, reach, sales · effort medium

**How:** Tag each planned post TOFU, MOFU or BOFU in the content plan.

**Backed by:** [Weekly mix 4 : 2 : 1](../topics/growth.md#growth-weekly-4-2-1), [Stories sell twice a week, nurture the rest](../topics/growth.md#growth-stories-nurture-sell), [Weekly lead magnet into an owned list](../topics/growth.md#growth-lead-magnet-series), [Caption: hook line, story, CTA, 3–5 tags](../topics/text.md#text-caption-structure), [Lead-magnet CTA over a recap strip](../topics/growth.md#l11-lead-magnet-recap-cta) · sources L08

## Rarely sell in organic content
<a id="rarely-sell"></a>

Organic content builds trust; selling happens elsewhere (long form, email, the bio).

**Looks like:** Reels end on a takeaway question or nothing at all. The offer lives in the bio and the newsletter.

**Good at:** trust; pure audience growth; no CTA fatigue

**Weak at:** few leads; slow to monetise

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, carousel · niches all · goals trust, follows · effort low

**How:** Use conversation or share CTAs only. Selling is in the bio line 3.

**Backed by:** [Trust before transactions](../topics/business.md#biz-trust-before-transactions), [Content funnel: top, middle, bottom](../topics/growth.md#growth-content-funnel), [Short form = awareness, long = conversion](../topics/growth.md#growth-short-awareness-long-conversion), [Ads work better with organic presence](../topics/business.md#biz-ads-need-organic), [CTA that doesn't sell: your takeaway](../topics/growth.md#growth-takeaway-cta) · sources L05, L07

## Mixing
Every reel can carry a free keyword (not a sale) while selling stays weekly, so the two are compatible when the freebie is free.

## Rule of thumb
Comments and lead lists: every reel. Balanced growth plus sales: weekly rhythm. Pure brand building: rarely sell.
